classification.difficultyReason: Represent constrained roots algebraically and prove two coefficient identities.

content.prompt: The polynomial equation $x^4+px^3+qx^2+rx+s=0$ has two roots that sum to zero, and another two roots that are reciprocals of each other. Show that:

answer.worked:
Let the roots be $\alpha,-\alpha,\beta,\dfrac1\beta$.

The product of the roots gives
$$\begin{aligned}s&=\alpha(-\alpha)\beta\frac1\beta\\s&=-\alpha^2.\end{aligned}$$
The sum of the pairwise products gives
$$\begin{aligned}q&=-\alpha^2+\alpha\beta+\frac\alpha\beta-\alpha\beta-\frac\alpha\beta+1\\q&=-\alpha^2+1\\q&=1+s.\end{aligned}$$

Let the roots be $\alpha,-\alpha,\beta,\dfrac1\beta$. Their sum and product give
$$\begin{aligned}\beta+\frac1\beta&=-p,\\-\alpha^2&=s.\end{aligned}$$
The sum of the triple products is $-r$:
$$\begin{aligned}-r&=-\alpha^2\beta-\frac{\alpha^2}{\beta}-\alpha+\alpha\\-r&=-\alpha^2\left(\beta+\frac1\beta\right)\\-r&=s(-p)\\-r&=-sp\\r&=ps.\end{aligned}$$
